German settlers planted vines in the 1840s; the modern era began with Hermann Seifried (1973) and Tim and Judy Finn at Neudorf (1978), whose Moutere Chardonnay is one of the country's best.
appellations.terroir: Sheltered by mountains on three sides; high sunshine and moderate rain. Moutere gravel-clays (weathered, iron-rich) contrast with the stony Waimea Plains.
appellations.nerd_note: Neudorf's Moutere Chardonnay comes from vines on the clay-gravel 'Moutere Gravels', which hold water and give a dense, mineral wine.

appellations.name: Marlborough
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc (about 80 percent), Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Riesling
appellations.summary:
Marlborough, at the north-eastern tip of the South Island, has about 32,000 ha of vines, 73 percent of New Zealand's vineyard, and more than 1,100 vineyards. Sheep grazed its flat Wairau Valley until 1973, when Montana planted vines at Brancott against advice that the region was too cold and dry. Its first Sauvignon Blanc, from the 1979 vintage, showed something new: intensely aromatic wine, with passion fruit, gooseberry and fresh-cut grass, and searing acidity. Hunter's success in London in 1986 and Cloudy Bay's launch in 1985 brought world attention, and Marlborough Sauvignon became one of the most successful wine styles of the modern era.

The region has three main sub-areas. The Wairau Valley, along the Wairau River, has stony, free-draining alluvial soils on its northern side (Rapaura) that give the classic tropical style. The Southern Valleys (Brancott, Omaka, Fairhall, Ben Morven, Waihopai), on clay-rich soils, give more textured Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. The Awatere Valley to the south-east, higher, windier and cooler, gives a leaner, more herbaceous and saline style. Producers such as Dog Point, Greywacke, Clos Henri, Te Whare Ra, Seresin and Churton show that Marlborough can also make complex, barrel-fermented and wild-yeast Sauvignon, serious Pinot Noir and traditional-method sparkling. The flip side is heavy reliance on one grape: the region produced a record crop in 2025 and growers face pressure to diversify.
appellations.terroir: Very sunny (about 2,400 hours a year), dry (about 650 mm of rain) and with big swings between warm days and cool nights. Soils are young alluvial gravels, silts and clays laid down by the Wairau, Awatere and their tributaries.
appellations.nerd_note: Ivan Sutherland and James Healy, who left Cloudy Bay to found Dog Point, make Section 94, a barrel-fermented Sauvignon Blanc named after a land-survey section.

appellations.name: Canterbury
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The Canterbury GI covers the broad province around Christchurch, from the Canterbury Plains to Banks Peninsula. French settlers planted vines at Akaroa in 1840, and Lincoln University's research in the 1970s showed the plains could ripen cool-climate grapes. Today almost all quality vineyards are in North Canterbury, a separate GI inside it.
appellations.terroir: Cool, dry and windy, with the nor'wester (a hot, dry foehn wind) a defining feature.

appellations.name: North Canterbury
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris
appellations.summary: North Canterbury, registered in 2020, covers the hills north of Christchurch, including the Waipara Valley and the limestone country around Waikari. With about 1,540 ha, it is a source of some of New Zealand's most intellectually interesting wines: Pyramid Valley's and Bell Hill's limestone-grown Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, and Pegasus Bay's Riesling and Pinot.
appellations.terroir: Warm, dry summers and long autumns protected from easterly sea breezes by the Teviotdale Hills; limestone, clay and gravels.
appellations.nerd_note: The limestone at Waikari and Weka Pass is rare in New Zealand, which is one reason Burgundy-obsessed growers chose it.

appellations.name: Waipara Valley
appellations.grapes: Riesling, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A small, warm valley about an hour north of Christchurch, registered as a GI in 2018 and sitting within North Canterbury. Pegasus Bay, founded by the Donaldson family in 1985, made its name for Riesling (in dry to botrytised styles) and Pinot Noir; Black Estate, Greystone and Mountford followed. The valley is sheltered from cool easterlies by the Teviotdale Hills, so it ripens grapes well for its latitude.
appellations.terroir: Glacial gravels and clay loams on the valley floor, with limestone-rich clays on the slopes; hot dry summers and the nor'wester wind.

appellations.name: Waitaki Valley North Otago
match: Waitaki Valley North Otago / Waitaki Valley
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: One of New Zealand's newest and most marginal regions, in the Waitaki River valley around Kurow and Duntroon, registered in 2018. Its first vines went in around 2001. Limestone outcrops and a cold, frost-prone climate attracted growers such as Jim Jerram (Ostler) and Michelle Richardson. With fewer than 50 ha, it makes taut Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and schist gravels with windblown loess; very cool, with a short season and frost risk.

appellations.name: Central Otago
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir (about 70 to 80 percent), Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary:
Central Otago is often called the world's most southerly commercial wine region, at around 45 degrees south (vineyards near Sarmiento in Argentine Patagonia, at about 45.6 degrees, now contest the title), and its Pinot Noir is New Zealand's most famous red. It is a dramatic place: dry brown hills of schist, rivers and lakes, gold-rush ruins and snow-capped mountains. Jean Désiré Feraud planted vines at Clyde in 1864, but the modern industry began in the 1970s and 1980s with Rolfe and Lois Mills at Rippon on Lake Wanaka (1975) and Alan Brady at Gibbston Valley (first commercial wine in 1987). It now has about 2,100 ha and more than 230 vineyards.

The climate is semi-continental: hot, dry summer days, cold nights and frost in spring and autumn, so vineyards occupy slopes and terraces that drain cold air. Pinot Noir here is vivid and dark-fruited, with spice and fine tannin. Sub-regions differ. Gibbston, in the Kawarau Gorge near Queenstown, is the coolest and highest; Bannockburn (a registered GI since 2022) and the Cromwell Basin (Bendigo, Pisa, Lowburn) are the warmest and give the most powerful wines; Alexandra is dry and continental; Wanaka is lakeside and cool. Felton Road (Bannockburn), Rippon (Wanaka), Burn Cottage, Prophet's Rock (Bendigo) and Two Paddocks are among the leaders.
appellations.terroir: Schist-derived gravels and loess (windblown silt), very low rainfall (often under 400 mm), high sunshine and big temperature swings. Most vineyards are irrigated.
appellations.nerd_note: Rippon's vineyard on the shore of Lake Wanaka is one of the most photographed in the world; Nick Mills farms it biodynamically.

appellations.name: Bannockburn
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling, Pinot Gris
appellations.summary: The most recent New Zealand wine GI, registered in February 2022, covering a small, warm sub-region of Central Otago on the southern bank of the Kawarau River near Cromwell. Gold miners sluiced its hills in the 1860s and 1870s, leaving the 'Cairnmuir' sluicings, an eerie landscape of cliffs and tailings. Stewart Elms planted Felton Road here in 1991 and 1992; with Mount Difficulty, Akarua and Carrick it made Bannockburn's ripe, structured, mineral Pinot Noir the most celebrated in the region.
appellations.terroir: One of the warmest and driest corners of Central Otago, on schist-derived gravels, loess and clays over sandstone, at about 220 to 400 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Felton Road's Block 3 and Block 5 Pinot Noirs come from parcels of the original Elms planting, on deeper loess and on a more exposed terrace respectively.

appellations.name: Greater Cape
appellations.summary: An overarching unit created after a 2019 proposal that groups the Western Cape, Northern Cape and Eastern Cape geographical units, so that wines blended across provincial lines (for example Western Cape and Orange River fruit) can carry a Cape origin.

appellations.name: Western Cape
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Colombard, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The Western Cape geographical unit holds almost all of South Africa's wine grapes. 'WO Western Cape' on a label means a blend from two or more of its regions, and many large brands use it.

appellations.name: Northern Cape
appellations.grapes: Colombard, Chenin Blanc, Muscat d'Alexandrie, Pinotage
appellations.summary: The Northern Cape geographical unit covers the irrigated vineyards of the Orange River and the high Karoo around Sutherland. Most fruit goes to large co-operative cellars. Its best-known wine area is the Central Orange River district around Upington, where vineyards on islands in the river are cooled by the water.

appellations.name: Eastern Cape
appellations.summary: The Eastern Cape was designated a geographical unit in 2009. Its only ward is St Francis Bay, on the coast west of Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha). Its few vineyards face rain spread through the year, unlike the Western Cape's dry summers.

appellations.name: KwaZulu-Natal
appellations.grapes: Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: KwaZulu-Natal, designated in 2005, stretches from Greytown to the Midlands at up to about 1,500 m. Its summer rainfall makes viticulture difficult; it contains the Lions River and Central Drakensberg districts.

appellations.name: Free State
appellations.summary: The Free State geographical unit has one ward, Rietrivier FS, on the Riet River near Jacobsdal. Grapes there are mostly grown for local co-operative wine and brandy.

appellations.name: Limpopo
appellations.summary: A geographical unit covering South Africa's northernmost province; it has no regions, districts or wards on the February 2026 list. Summer rainfall and subtropical heat make viticulture marginal.

appellations.name: North West
appellations.summary: A geographical unit covering the North West province; it has no regions, districts or wards on the February 2026 list. Summer rainfall and highveld frost make viticulture marginal.

appellations.name: Cape Coast
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: An overarching region that combines the Coastal Region and Cape South Coast, allowing blends of, say, Stellenbosch and Elgin fruit to name a coastal origin. It is a recent addition to the Wine of Origin hierarchy, sitting between the Western Cape unit and the regions.

appellations.name: Coastal Region
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Pinotage, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The Coastal Region includes South Africa's best-known districts: Cape Town, Stellenbosch, Paarl, Franschhoek, Wellington, Swartland, Tulbagh, Darling and Lutzville Valley. 'WO Coastal Region' usually indicates a blend across several of them.

appellations.name: Cape South Coast
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Shiraz
appellations.summary: The cool southern coastal region from Elgin to Plettenberg Bay, home to Walker Bay and its Hemel-en-Aarde wards, Elim and Elgin. Most of its vineyards are young, planted from the 1970s onward, and it is South Africa's main source of Pinot Noir.

appellations.name: Breede River Valley
appellations.summary: The inland region of the Breedekloof, Worcester and Robertson districts, warm and irrigated, the source of a large share of South Africa's wine and brandy. The region crushes a large share of South Africa's grapes, most of it through co-operative cellars.

appellations.name: Klein Karoo
appellations.grapes: Muscat, Touriga Nacional, Chenin Blanc, Colombard
appellations.summary: The semi-arid valley along Route 62 from Montagu to the Langkloof, known for Calitzdorp's fortified wines, Muscadel and potstill brandy. Vines grow in kloofs and river valleys between ostrich farms.

appellations.name: Olifants River
appellations.summary: The region along the Olifants River from Citrusdal to Lutzville, with old mountain vineyards at Piekenierskloof and large irrigated cellars at Vredendal. It is citrus and rooibos country.

appellations.name: Karoo-Hoogland
appellations.summary: A high-plateau region in the Northern Cape whose only district is Sutherland-Karoo, around one of South Africa's coldest towns. Its vineyards, at around 1,500 m, are the highest in South Africa.

appellations.name: Cape West Coast
appellations.summary: A subregion grouping the Atlantic-facing Darling and Lutzville Valley districts, St Helena Bay and the Bamboes Bay and Lamberts Bay wards, all cooled by the Benguela current. It was proposed in 2019 and appears on the February 2026 list of production areas.

appellations.name: Cape Town
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Muscat de Frontignan
appellations.summary: A district named after the city, combining the wards of Constantia, Durbanville, Hout Bay and Philadelphia and the vineyards of the Cape Peninsula, including Cape Point. At its farthest point it is 36 km from the city centre. It replaced the former Cape Point and Tygerberg districts, which no longer appear on the February 2026 list.
appellations.terroir: Sea on three sides, Table Mountain sandstone and granite, and the cooling south-easter; one of the coolest districts in South Africa.

appellations.name: Constantia
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Muscat de Frontignan
appellations.summary:
Constantia is the cradle of Cape wine and the source of one of history's most famous sweet wines. Simon van der Stel was granted the land in 1685 and planted a large vineyard on the eastern slopes of the Constantiaberg; after his death in 1712 the estate was split into Groot Constantia, Klein Constantia and Bergvliet. From 1778 Hendrik Cloete made an unfortified wine from late-picked Muscat de Frontignan (with some Pontac, Muscadel and Chenin) that European kings, Napoleon on St Helena, Jane Austen's characters and Baudelaire's verse all celebrated. Phylloxera and the end of imperial preference ended it in the late nineteenth century; Klein Constantia revived it as Vin de Constance in 1986, followed by Groot Constantia (Grand Constance) and Buitenverwachting.

Today the ward's handful of estates, now surrounded by expensive suburbs, make some of South Africa's best Sauvignon Blanc and Sauvignon-Sémillon blends, aided by sea air from False Bay a few kilometres away. The ward also carries a modern history: under the Group Areas Act, Constantia was declared a white area in 1961 and families of colour were forcibly removed; the Solomon family won back its land through a restitution claim in 2010.
appellations.terroir: East- and south-east-facing slopes of the Constantiaberg on decomposed granite and sandstone, about 1,000 mm of rain a year, and a mean February temperature of about 20.6 degrees C; cool sea breezes from False Bay.
appellations.nerd_note: Klein Constantia's Vin de Constance bottle reproduces a squat, hand-blown 18th-century design, and it is aged about four years before release.

appellations.name: Durbanville
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinotage
appellations.summary: Rolling wheat-and-vine country on the northern edge of Cape Town, whose hills catch Atlantic breezes and night-time mist. Durbanville made its name for pungent, green-fruited Sauvignon Blanc and soft Merlot, and many farms (Diemersdal, Meerendal, Altydgedacht) have been in the same families for generations.
appellations.terroir: Deep, red, decomposed granite and shale soils that hold water, allowing dry farming; vineyards up to about 380 m.

appellations.name: Philadelphia
appellations.summary: A small ward north of Durbanville around the village of Philadelphia, on hills up to about 260 m within sight of the Atlantic, known for structured Bordeaux-style reds. Capaia, with its hilltop winery, is the ward's best-known estate.
appellations.terroir: Weathered shale and granite; cool Atlantic influence with large day-night differences.

appellations.name: Hout Bay
appellations.summary: One of South Africa's smallest wards, in the steep valley behind Hout Bay harbour on the Cape Peninsula, with a few hectares of vines. Its vines grow on steep slopes in sight of the Atlantic.
appellations.terroir: Steep granite and sandstone slopes facing the Atlantic.

appellations.name: Stellenbosch
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Merlot, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc
appellations.summary:
Stellenbosch is South Africa's most famous wine district and its intellectual centre. The town, founded by Simon van der Stel in 1679 and shaded by oaks, has the country's only university degree in viticulture and oenology, the Elsenburg agricultural college and the Nietvoorbij research institute. More than 200 producers farm the district's slopes, from historic estates to modern wineries.

Its strength is red wine, above all Cabernet Sauvignon and Bordeaux-style blends, which gain structure and freshness from the district's granite mountains and the cooling south-easter off False Bay. Meerlust Rubicon (first made in 1980), Kanonkop Paul Sauer, Vergelegen V and Rust en Vrede's estate blend are classics, and Kanonkop's Pinotage, from vines planted in the 1950s, is the reference for the country's own grape. Old-vine Chenin Blanc from the Bottelary and Helderberg areas and Chardonnay from the higher slopes are equally serious.

The district is divided into eight wards: Banghoek, Bottelary, Devon Valley, Jonkershoek Valley, Papegaaiberg, Polkadraai Hills, Simonsberg-Stellenbosch and Vlottenburg. Much of the best-known land, including the Helderberg slopes around Somerset West (Vergelegen, Rust en Vrede, Waterford, Ernie Els), lies outside any ward and is labelled simply 'Stellenbosch'. The Stellenbosch Wine Route, founded in 1971, was South Africa's first.
appellations.terroir: Mountains on three sides (Simonsberg, Jonkershoek, Helderberg) and False Bay to the south; about 600 to 800 mm of rain in the valley, more on the mountains. Decomposed granite on the higher slopes, Table Mountain sandstone higher still, and Malmesbury shale and alluvium on the lower ground to the west.
appellations.nerd_note: Stellenbosch's oak-lined streets are a result of Van der Stel's order to plant oaks in the 1680s; the university's experimental farm at Welgevallen is where Perold bred Pinotage in 1925.

appellations.name: Simonsberg-Stellenbosch
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage, Merlot, Shiraz, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The southern and western slopes of the granite Simonsberg (1,390 m) north-east of Stellenbosch, one of the most prestigious wards in South Africa and among the first to be demarcated. Its well-drained, red decomposed-granite soils, altitude and afternoon sea breezes give structured, long-lived Cabernet and Bordeaux blends and the country's most famous Pinotage. Kanonkop, Rustenberg, Thelema, Tokara, Warwick, Delheim and Uitkyk are all here.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite (red Hutton and Clovelly soils) at about 150 to 500 m; south- and west-facing slopes catch the False Bay breeze.
appellations.nerd_note: The official schedule of February 2026 misspells the ward as 'Simonsberg-Stellenbosh'.

appellations.name: Jonkershoek Valley
appellations.summary: A narrow, steep-sided valley running south-east from Stellenbosch town into the Jonkershoek mountains, one of the wettest and most enclosed parts of the district. Morning shade and late sun give long, slow ripening; Stark-Condé and Neil Ellis's Jonkershoek vineyards make fine, fresh Cabernet.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite and sandstone colluvium on steep slopes; about 1,000 mm or more of rain.

appellations.name: Banghoek
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A high mountain bowl at the top of the Helshoogte Pass between Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, surrounded by the Simonsberg, Jonkershoek and Groot Drakenstein ranges. Cooler and wetter than the valley below, it gives fresh, elegant Bordeaux varieties and Chardonnay.
appellations.terroir: Granite and sandstone soils at about 400 to 600 m; high rainfall.

appellations.name: Bottelary
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: The Bottelary Hills north-west of Stellenbosch, a ridge of granite with views to Table Mountain, is old-vine Chenin and Pinotage country. Bellevue, in these hills, made the Pinotage that won the 1959 Cape Wine Show, and Kaapzicht, Hartenberg, Mooiplaas and Bellevue still farm old bush vines.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite on the upper slopes and shale lower down; open to Atlantic breezes from the west.

appellations.name: Devon Valley
appellations.grapes: Merlot, Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: A small, sheltered valley north-west of Stellenbosch town between the Bottelary Hills and Papegaaiberg, known for Merlot and Pinotage on granite and shale soils. It is one of the most sheltered parts of the district, and its small size keeps it a district of family estates.
appellations.terroir: Granite-derived soils, sheltered from wind.

appellations.name: Papegaaiberg
appellations.summary: A small hill just west of Stellenbosch town, the 'parrot mountain' where early settlers practised shooting at a wooden parrot. The Bergkelder, Distell's (now Heineken Beverages') maturation cellar, is tunnelled into its slopes.
appellations.terroir: Granite and shale on a low ridge.

appellations.name: Polkadraai Hills
appellations.grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Hills west of Stellenbosch near the R310 and Polkadraai Road, open to cool breezes from both False Bay and the Atlantic. Johan Reyneke farms biodynamically here, and the ward's sandy granite soils give fresh, fragrant Syrah and Chenin.
appellations.terroir: Sandy, decomposed granite over clay at about 100 to 300 m.

appellations.name: Vlottenburg
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: A ward south-west of Stellenbosch town around the Vlottenburg railway halt and the Eerste River, where cooling False Bay winds reach the vines in the afternoon. Its old co-operative cellar is now Stellenbosch Hills, and the ward's Bordeaux varieties and Chenin Blanc benefit from afternoon sea breezes.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial and shale-derived soils on gentle slopes.

appellations.name: Paarl
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Paarl, named after the pearl-like granite domes of Paarl Mountain, lies north of Stellenbosch along the Berg River. It was the seat of the KWV from 1918, which made it the administrative capital of the industry for most of the twentieth century, and home to Nederburg, whose annual auction (from 1975) became the country's most important wine sale. The district is warmer than Stellenbosch and its Shiraz, Cabernet, Pinotage and Chenin are generous and ripe. Its wards are Simonsberg-Paarl, Voor-Paardeberg and Agter-Paarl.
appellations.terroir: Granite domes and slopes, with alluvial soils along the Berg River; the valley needs supplementary irrigation in hot summers while the eastern slopes hold water.

appellations.name: Simonsberg-Paarl
appellations.summary: The north-eastern slopes of the Simonsberg facing Paarl, on decomposed granite. Glen Carlou, Plaisir de Merle, Backsberg and Rupert & Rothschild make Bordeaux blends and Chardonnay here. It is warmer than the Simonsberg-Stellenbosch side of the mountain, and its reds are correspondingly riper.
appellations.terroir: Granite-derived soils on north- and east-facing slopes; warmer than the Stellenbosch side of the mountain.

appellations.name: Voor-Paardeberg
appellations.summary: The southern and eastern side ('voor', in front of) the Paardeberg, the granite massif between Paarl and the Swartland. Old dry-land bush vines of Chenin, Cinsault and Shiraz supply many of the Cape's new-wave winemakers.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite over clay, dry farmed; warm and windy.

appellations.name: Agter-Paarl
appellations.grapes: Shiraz, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: The country 'behind' (agter) Paarl Mountain to the west, towards the Swartland, where Fairview's Charles Back farms goats and vines and makes Rhône-style wines and cheese. It is warmer and drier than the Paarl valley.
appellations.terroir: Granite-derived soils and shale on gentle slopes; warm and dry.

appellations.name: Franschhoek
appellations.grapes: Sémillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Franschhoek, the 'French corner', is the valley where the VOC settled Huguenot refugees after 1688. It is enclosed on three sides by the Groot Drakenstein and Franschhoek mountains, with the Berg River rising at its head. The district holds some of South Africa's oldest vineyards, including Sémillon (and the rare Sémillon Gris) planted in the early twentieth century, and it is a centre of Cap Classique and of the Cape's restaurant culture. The Huguenot Monument (1948) stands at the head of the town.
appellations.terroir: Sandy alluvium on the valley floor and decomposed sandstone and granite on the slopes; enclosed, warmer by day and colder at night than Stellenbosch, with snow on the peaks in winter.
appellations.nerd_note: Boekenhoutskloof's Sémillon comes from vines planted in 1902 and 1942, among the oldest Sémillon in the world.

appellations.name: Wellington
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A district north of Paarl at the foot of the Hawequa mountains, about 45 minutes from Cape Town. It supplies more than 85 percent of South Africa's vine cuttings from its nurseries, and its 30 or so producers range from historic estates to Diemersfontein, which created 'coffee Pinotage' in 2001. Its five wards (Blouvlei, Bovlei, Groenberg, Limietberg and Mid-Berg River) were added recently.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial terraces along the Berg River and granite and sandstone foothills; snow on the peaks in winter, cooler nights than the coast.

appellations.name: Blouvlei
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of the Wellington district on the slopes and plain below the Hawequa mountains. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

appellations.name: Bovlei
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of Wellington in the upper Bovlei valley towards the Bainskloof Pass, home of the historic Bovlei co-operative cellar (1907). It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

appellations.name: Groenberg
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward around the Groenberg hill north of Wellington town, with granite soils. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

appellations.name: Limietberg
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward on the lower slopes of the Limietberg (Hawequa) range east of Wellington, where mountain foothills create cooler mesoclimates. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

appellations.name: Mid-Berg River
appellations.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward on the alluvial terraces of the middle Berg River between Wellington and Paarl. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

appellations.name: Swartland
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Grenache, Cinsault, Pinotage, Mourvèdre, Palomino
appellations.summary:
The Swartland, the 'black land', takes its name from the renosterbos (rhino bush) that once darkened its rolling wheatfields north of Cape Town. For most of its history it grew grain and supplied big co-operatives with high-yielding grapes. That changed when Charles Back of Fairview and Spice Route began buying land here in the late 1990s and a young winemaker, Eben Sadie, found old, dry-farmed bush vines of Chenin Blanc, Grenache, Cinsault and Syrah on the Paardeberg. His Columella (2000) and Palladius (2002) showed what they could do.

A generation followed: Chris and Andrea Mullineux, Adi Badenhorst at Kalmoesfontein, Callie Louw at Porseleinberg, Craig Hawkins (Testalonga), Lammershoek, David and Nadia Sadie, Donovan Rall. Their Swartland Revolution festival (2010 to 2015) and the Swartland Independent Producers association, which sets rules on natural winemaking and regional sourcing, made the district shorthand for South Africa's new wave: whole-bunch Syrah, old-vine Chenin blends aged in old foudres and concrete, and skin-contact whites. The district also has eight wards, from the Paardeberg granite to the schist of the Riebeek and Porseleinberg slopes.
appellations.terroir: Warm and dry (400 to 600 mm of rain), with mostly dry-farmed bush vines. Soils include decomposed granite (Paardeberg), Malmesbury shale and schist (Kasteelberg, Porseleinberg) and iron-rich koffieklip.
appellations.nerd_note: Sadie's 'Old Vineyard Series' bottles single old vineyards from across the Cape, each label naming the site, such as Skerpioen, Mev. Kirsten and 'T Voetpad.

appellations.name: Paardeberg/Perdeberg
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Grenache, Cinsault, Mourvèdre
appellations.summary: The granite massif of the Paardeberg (Perdeberg in Afrikaans), on the border of the Swartland and Paarl, is the spiritual home of the Swartland revival. Eben Sadie's farm and cellar, A.A. Badenhorst's Kalmoesfontein and many old Chenin and Cinsault vineyards are here. Its decomposed granite holds winter rain, so old bush vines survive without irrigation.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite over clay on rounded hills; warm, dry and windy.

appellations.name: Paardeberg South
appellations.summary: The southern foothills of the Paardeberg, separated as their own ward, with granite soils similar to the main Paardeberg ward. Old dry-farmed bush vines of Chenin Blanc and Cinsault here supply several new-wave Swartland labels.

appellations.name: Piket-Bo-Berg
appellations.summary: A high plateau on top of the Piketberg mountain, north of the Swartland at about 600 to 700 m, cooler than the valleys below; the WOSA text calls it Piketberg-Bo-Berg.

appellations.name: Porseleinberg
appellations.summary: A ward named after the 'porcelain mountain' between Riebeek-Kasteel and the Berg River, whose blue-grey schist soils Boekenhoutskloof chose for its Porseleinberg Syrah, farmed organically by Callie Louw since the first vintage in 2010.
appellations.terroir: Malmesbury schist with very little topsoil; warm and dry.

appellations.name: Riebeekberg
appellations.summary: The slopes of the Kasteelberg around the villages of Riebeek-Kasteel and Riebeek-West, where the Mullineuxs farm their Roundstone vineyard on schist and iron-rich soils. Many of the Swartland's new-wave producers source fruit here.
appellations.terroir: Schist, shale and koffieklip (iron-rich ferricrete).

appellations.name: Riebeeksrivier
appellations.summary: A newer ward along the Riebeeks River valley below the Kasteelberg, on shale and alluvial soils. It lies between the Riebeekberg and Porseleinberg wards in the heart of the new-wave Swartland.

appellations.name: Malmesbury
appellations.summary: The ward around Malmesbury, the Swartland's main town, among wheatfields on Malmesbury shale. Its old dryland bush vines of Chenin Blanc and Pinotage were long sold to the Swartland Winery co-operative and are now sought by smaller producers too.

appellations.name: St Helena Bay
appellations.summary: A coastal ward on St Helena Bay on the Atlantic, the fishing coast north of Saldanha, now grouped in the Cape West Coast subregion though listed under the Swartland district.
appellations.terroir: Sandy soils, cold Benguela fog and wind.

appellations.name: Tulbagh
appellations.summary: A horseshoe-shaped valley enclosed by the Groot Winterhoek, Witzenberg and Obiekwaberg mountains, about 90 minutes north of Cape Town. Cold air pools on the valley floor at night (a 'cold trap'), giving large day-night temperature swings. Tulbagh's Church Street has 32 national monuments, many restored after the 1969 earthquake. The valley is known for Shiraz and Rhône blends and for Cap Classique pioneer Krone (Twee Jonge Gezellen).
appellations.terroir: A former lake basin with varied alluvial and sandstone soils.

appellations.name: Darling
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Darling, an hour north of Cape Town on the west coast, is famous for spring wild flowers and for cool Sauvignon Blanc. Its Groenekloof ward is one of the closest in South Africa to the cold Atlantic.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite hills catching Atlantic fog and wind.

appellations.name: Groenekloof
appellations.summary: The Darling ward nearest the Atlantic, whose Sauvignon Blanc, cooled by sea breezes and fog, spearheaded the area's development. Groote Post's Peter Pentz farms here. Neil Ellis was an early buyer of its cool-climate fruit.
appellations.terroir: Granite-derived soils on hills a few kilometres from the sea.

appellations.name: Lutzville Valley
appellations.summary: A district near the mouth of the Olifants River with large irrigated vineyards, including the Lutzville co-operative. It is one of the most northerly coastal wine districts in South Africa, cooled by the Atlantic and dependent on irrigation from the Olifants River.

appellations.name: Koekenaap
appellations.summary: A cool, sea-influenced ward close to the Atlantic in the Lutzville Valley, where grapes ripen slowly in coastal fog. It is one of the most northerly coastal wards in South Africa.

appellations.name: Bamboes Bay
appellations.summary: One of South Africa's smallest wards, on the Atlantic coast north of Lamberts Bay, where Fryer's Cove's vineyards lie a few hundred metres from the ocean. Its Sauvignon Blanc is lean and saline.
appellations.terroir: Sandy and limestone soils, cold Benguela fog.

appellations.name: Lamberts Bay
appellations.summary: A coastal ward around the fishing town of Lamberts Bay, cooled by the Benguela current. Its vineyards, among the coolest on the west coast, mostly grow Sauvignon Blanc.

appellations.name: Elgin
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Shiraz
appellations.summary: Elgin is a high basin about an hour east of Cape Town, ringed by the Hottentots Holland mountains, which grew most of South Africa's apples before its farmers began planting vines in the late 1980s. Its altitude (200 to 800 m), cloud and proximity to the sea make it one of the coolest districts in South Africa, and its Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir are taut and fine. Paul Cluver, Oak Valley, Iona, Richard Kershaw and Shannon lead.
appellations.terroir: Table Mountain sandstone and Bokkeveld shale; cool summers, about 1,000 mm of rain.

appellations.name: Walker Bay
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage, Shiraz
appellations.summary: The district around the whale-watching town of Hermanus, best known for the Hemel-en-Aarde ('heaven and earth') valley, where Tim Hamilton Russell planted Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in 1975 and made the Cape's first serious Burgundy-style wines. Walker Bay now has seven wards: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge, Bot River, Stanford Foothills, Springfontein Rim and Sunday's Glen. Its Pinotage is also highly regarded.
appellations.terroir: Weathered Bokkeveld shale and decomposed granite; strong maritime influence and wind from Walker Bay.

appellations.name: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinotage, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The lowest of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards, closest to the sea at Hermanus. Hamilton Russell Vineyards (1975) and Bouchard Finlayson (1989, a venture between Peter Finlayson and Burgundy's Paul Bouchard) established South African Pinot Noir and Chardonnay here; the clay-rich shale soils give wines of structure and minerality.
appellations.terroir: Bokkeveld shale with high clay content, stony; cool sea breezes, about 750 mm of rain.

appellations.name: Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah
appellations.summary: The middle section of the Hemel-en-Aarde, further inland and slightly warmer, on lighter granite-derived and shale soils. Newton Johnson, La Vierge, Restless River and Storm make some of the country's most elegant Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: Decomposed granite and shale; more sheltered than the lower valley.

appellations.name: Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge
appellations.summary: The highest and furthest inland of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards, at the top of the valley around 300 m and above, with cooler nights. Creation and Domaine des Dieux are here, and Chris and Suzaan Alheit's Hemelrand farm is nearby.
appellations.terroir: Shale and sandstone with some granite; cool and windy.

appellations.name: Bot River
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The gateway to Walker Bay, from the Bot River lagoon into the foothills of the Groenlandberg and Babylonstoren ranges, bordering the Kogelberg Biosphere. Beaumont, in the village, has old Chenin and Pinotage; Gabrielskloof, Wildekrans and Barton are nearby. Afternoon winds blow up the valley off the sea.
appellations.terroir: Mainly Bokkeveld shale (Glen Rosa and Klapmuts soils) and Table Mountain sandstone.

appellations.name: Stanford Foothills
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A ward on the foothills of the Kleinrivier mountains above the village of Stanford, east of the Hemel-en-Aarde. It was registered as a ward recently, alongside Springfontein Rim and Sunday's Glen, as Walker Bay's vineyards spread east from the Hemel-en-Aarde.

appellations.name: Springfontein Rim
appellations.summary: A small coastal ward near Stanford around the Springfontein estate, close to the sea on limestone-influenced soils. The Springfontein estate, owned by a German family, grows Chenin Blanc and Pinotage on limestone-influenced coastal soils there.

appellations.name: Sunday's Glen
appellations.summary: The easternmost Walker Bay ward, beyond Stanford, a cool coastal site. Like the other new Walker Bay wards, it relies on the cooling influence of the Atlantic and on Bokkeveld shale and sandstone soils, which suit Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

appellations.name: Cape Agulhas
appellations.summary: The district at Africa's southern tip; almost all its vines are in the Elim ward. Strong winds and a cool ripening season produce pungent Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon.

appellations.name: Elim
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Shiraz, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Elim's vineyards lie near Cape Agulhas, Africa's southernmost point, around the Moravian mission village of Elim, founded in 1824 and a national monument. Strong summer winds and a very cool ripening season give pungent, mineral Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon and peppery Shiraz.
appellations.terroir: Ferricrete, shale and sandstone soils; constant wind off the sea.

appellations.name: Overberg
appellations.summary: A broad district of wheatfields and mountains east of Elgin, with wards at Elandskloof/Kaaimansgat, Greyton, Klein River, Shaw's Mountain and Theewater. Its cool, high wards produce Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

appellations.name: Elandskloof/Kaaimansgat
appellations.summary: A high, cool ward in the mountains near Villiersdorp. Bouchard Finlayson's Kaaimansgat ('crocodile's lair') Chardonnay comes from vineyards here at around 700 m. It is one of the coolest Chardonnay sites in the Cape.

appellations.name: Greyton
appellations.summary: A ward around the village of Greyton below the Riviersonderend mountains, where Samantha O'Keefe's Lismore Estate makes Chardonnay and Syrah. Its vineyards are cool and wind-exposed.

appellations.name: Klein River
appellations.summary: A ward near Stanford along the Klein River, where award-winning wines (Raka) have emerged. Its cool coastal climate suits Sauvignon Blanc and Bordeaux varieties.

appellations.name: Shaw's Mountain
appellations.summary: A recently added Overberg ward on the mountain slopes between Caledon and the Hemel-en-Aarde. Its cool, elevated slopes are suited to Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

appellations.name: Theewater
appellations.summary: A ward near the Theewaterskloof Dam and Villiersdorp, at the edge of the Overberg's mountains. The area's growers mainly sell fruit to cellars elsewhere.

appellations.name: Swellendam
appellations.summary: A district around the historic town of Swellendam (1743), the third-oldest in South Africa, with wards Buffeljags, Malgas and Stormsvlei. Its warm, dry wards lie along the lower Breede River between Robertson and the coast.

appellations.name: Malgas
appellations.grapes: Syrah, Mourvèdre, Touriga Nacional, Chenin Blanc
appellations.summary: A pioneering ward on a stony plateau 80 km east of Cape Agulhas, about 70 m above the Breede River. David and Rita Trafford's Sijnn planted drought-tolerant Mediterranean varieties here; rainfall is only about 350 mm, moderated by sea breezes from the coast 15 km away.
appellations.terroir: Complex stony soils of shale and quartzite gravel.

appellations.name: Buffeljags
appellations.summary: A ward around the Buffeljags River and dam east of Swellendam. It sits in warm, dry country along the lower Breede River system, between the Robertson valley and the coast, and most of its grapes are sold in bulk.

appellations.name: Stormsvlei
appellations.summary: A ward west of Swellendam near the Riviersonderend, on the road between Robertson and the coast. Its vineyards benefit from cool air drifting up the river valley from the coast.

appellations.name: Plettenberg Bay
appellations.summary: The newest and furthest-east district on the Cape South Coast, in mountainous terrain about 20 km east of Plettenberg Bay. The first vines were planted in 2000 (Bramon, known for Cap Classique). Cool coastal climate and high-carbon soils suit Sauvignon Blanc and sparkling.

appellations.name: Still Bay
appellations.summary: A coastal district around Stilbaai on the Garden Route, with the Goukou River Valley ward. Its vineyards, close to the Indian Ocean, are cooled by sea breezes and grow mostly Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.

appellations.name: Goukou River Valley
appellations.summary: A ward along the Goukou River inland from Stilbaai. It is one of the most easterly coastal wine wards on the Garden Route, with a mild, wet maritime climate.

appellations.name: Lower Duivenhoks River
appellations.summary: A small district along the lower Duivenhoks River between Heidelberg and the coast at Witsand. Its few vineyards benefit from sea breezes off the Indian Ocean near Witsand.

appellations.name: Herbertsdale
appellations.summary: A stand-alone ward near the village of Herbertsdale inland from Mossel Bay. Its mild Garden Route climate, with rain through the year, suits white varieties such as Sauvignon Blanc.

appellations.name: Napier
appellations.summary: A stand-alone ward around the Overberg village of Napier, between Bredasdorp and Caledon. Like nearby Elim, it is cooled by winds off the sea near Africa's southern tip, which suits Sauvignon Blanc and Shiraz.

appellations.name: Breedekloof
appellations.summary: A district around Rawsonville in the upper Breede River and its tributaries, below the Du Toitskloof mountains. Its large co-operatives once sent most fruit to distillers; now cellars such as Badsberg, Slanghoek and Goudini bottle good-value Chenin, and its old vineyards are sought by Stellenbosch winemakers.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial valley soils on a bed of river stones; varied mesoclimates in side valleys.

appellations.name: Goudini
appellations.summary: A ward around Rawsonville in the Breedekloof. Its alluvial soils over river stones and the cooling effect of the surrounding mountains suit Chenin Blanc and Colombard, delivered mostly to the Goudini co-operative cellar.

appellations.name: Slanghoek
appellations.summary: The Slanghoek valley north-west of Rawsonville, under the Slanghoek mountains. The Slanghoek cellar, a former co-operative, makes the ward's best-known wines, including fortified Hanepoot (Muscat d'Alexandrie) and Chenin Blanc.

appellations.name: Worcester
appellations.summary: The Worcester district is the brandy capital of South Africa, with the largest distillery of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere, and a major source of bulk and branded wine. It has seven wards: Hex River Valley, Keeromsberg, Moordkuil, Nuy, Rooikrans, Scherpenheuvel and Stettyn.

appellations.name: Hex River Valley
appellations.summary: The Hex River Valley around De Doorns, South Africa's largest table-grape area, also grows wine grapes. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

appellations.name: Keeromsberg
appellations.summary: A ward named after the Keeromsberg mountain north of Worcester. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy. Grapes from here go mainly to the Worcester district's co-operatives and to the brandy distilleries that make Worcester South Africa's brandy capital; ward names are rarely used on bottles.

appellations.name: Moordkuil
appellations.summary: A ward of the Worcester district. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy. Grapes from here go mainly to the Worcester district's co-operatives and to the brandy distilleries that make Worcester South Africa's brandy capital; ward names are rarely used on bottles.

appellations.name: Nuy
appellations.summary: A small valley east of Worcester whose Nuy cellar is famous for fortified Muscadel. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

appellations.name: Rooikrans
appellations.summary: A ward of the Worcester district. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy. Grapes from here go mainly to the Worcester district's co-operatives and to the brandy distilleries that make Worcester South Africa's brandy capital; ward names are rarely used on bottles.

appellations.name: Scherpenheuvel
appellations.summary: A ward on the road between Worcester and Robertson near the Brandvlei Dam. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

appellations.name: Stettyn
appellations.summary: A ward in the Stettynskloof west of Worcester, home of the Stettyn cellar. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

appellations.name: Robertson
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Colombard, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Muscadel
appellations.summary: The 'valley of vines and roses' along the Breede River is the only part of the Cape with significant lime-rich soils, which also suit its many racehorse studs. Hot summers are tempered by south-easterly winds that bring moist air up the valley. Danie de Wet of De Wetshof pioneered Chardonnay here in the 1970s, and Graham Beck's Madeba farm built South Africa's leading Cap Classique house in the 1990s. The district has 14 wards.
appellations.terroir: Calcareous soils over limestone along the Breede, with alluvium; about 400 mm of rain, irrigation needed.

appellations.name: Agterkliphoogte
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward in the Agterkliphoogte valley near Robertson. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Ashton
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward around the town of Ashton at the foot of the Langeberg. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Boesmansrivier
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward along the Boesmans River near Bonnievale. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Bonnievale
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward around Bonnievale on the Breede River, known for dairy and wine co-operatives. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate.

appellations.name: Eilandia
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward on low-lying land along the Breede River between Robertson and Ashton. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Goedemoed
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Goree
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward west of Robertson town. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Klaasvoogds
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward in the foothills of the Langeberg north-east of Robertson. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Le Chasseur
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of the Robertson district north of the town. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: McGregor
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward around the village of McGregor, south of Robertson below the Riviersonderend mountains, cooler and drier than the valley floor. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate.

appellations.name: Vinkrivier
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward along the Vink River near McGregor. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Zandrivier
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Calitzdorp
appellations.grapes: Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barocca, Souzão, Muscat, Chenin Blanc
appellations.summary: A small Klein Karoo town that calls itself South Africa's port capital. The Nel cousins at Boplaas and De Krans, and Axe Hill, make fortified wines from Portuguese varieties in Cape Vintage, Cape Tawny and Cape Ruby styles, the names used since 'port' was retired under the EU agreement in 2012. Hot days, cold nights and low rainfall concentrate the grapes. Its ward is Groenfontein.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial and shale soils along the Gamka River; about 200 to 300 mm of rain.

appellations.name: Groenfontein
appellations.summary: A ward in the Groenfontein valley north of Calitzdorp, below the Swartberg. Its vineyards supply Calitzdorp's port-style producers with Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barocca and Muscat, ripened in a hot, dry valley enclosed by mountains.

appellations.name: Langeberg-Garcia
appellations.summary: A district along the Langeberg range around the Garcia Pass near Riversdale. Its few vineyards lie at the eastern end of the Langeberg, on the edge of the Klein Karoo, with a cooler, wetter climate than the valleys to the north.

appellations.name: Montagu
appellations.summary: A ward around the spa town of Montagu at the western gateway of the Klein Karoo, famous for its fortified Muscadel. Its Muscadel is made from red and white Muscat à Petits Grains, fortified to sweetness.

appellations.name: Tradouw
appellations.summary: A ward around Barrydale below the Tradouw Pass. Joubert-Tradauw makes Chardonnay and Shiraz here, in one of the Klein Karoo's coolest corners, influenced by air from the coast through the Tradouw Pass.

appellations.name: Tradouw Highlands
appellations.summary: A higher, cooler ward in the mountains above Barrydale, whose growers make fresh whites and Pinot Noir. Its vineyards, at about 500 to 600 m, are among the coolest in the Klein Karoo.

appellations.name: Upper Langkloof
appellations.summary: A high, cool ward in the apple-growing Langkloof valley around Haarlem in the far east of the Klein Karoo. Its cool climate suits Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

appellations.name: Outeniqua
appellations.summary: A ward in the Outeniqua mountains north of George, where vineyards on the Montagu Pass reach about 700 m. Its vineyards near George get rain through the year and cooler temperatures than the Klein Karoo valleys to the north.

appellations.name: Cango Valley
appellations.summary: A ward north of Oudtshoorn in the valley of the Cango Caves. It lies in the hot Oudtshoorn ostrich country.

appellations.name: Koo Plateau
appellations.summary: A high plateau north of Montagu at about 1,000 m, apple and pear country with a cool climate. Its cool upland climate attracts winemakers looking for fresh Chenin Blanc.

appellations.name: Citrusdal Mountain
appellations.summary: The mountain district above the Citrusdal valley, whose old, dry-farmed bush vines on sandstone are among the most prized in the new South Africa. Its ward is Piekenierskloof, and its high Skurfberg vineyards supply Chenin to Sadie, Alheit and others.
appellations.terroir: Sandy, Table Mountain sandstone soils at up to 1,000 m; dry and hot by day, cold at night.

appellations.name: Piekenierskloof
appellations.grapes: Grenache, Chenin Blanc, Palomino, Pinotage, Cinsault
appellations.summary: A high plateau above the Piekenierskloof Pass south of Citrusdal, with some of South Africa's oldest Grenache and Palomino vineyards. Dry-farmed bush vines on deep sand give perfumed, light-coloured Grenache and textured whites prized by Swartland and Stellenbosch winemakers.
appellations.terroir: Deep, sandy soils derived from sandstone at 600 to 750 m.

appellations.name: Citrusdal Valley
appellations.summary: The citrus-growing southern Olifants River valley around Citrusdal and Clanwilliam, irrigated from the Clanwilliam Dam. Its irrigated vineyards supply large cellars; the old dry-farmed vines that excite new-wave producers are in the mountains above.

appellations.name: Vredendal
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage
appellations.summary: The ward around Vredendal in the lower Olifants River, home to Namaqua Wines, one of the largest cellars in South Africa. Namaqua Wines, formed by merging the Vredendal and Spruitdrift co-operatives, is one of the country's largest producers of inexpensive bottled and boxed wine.

appellations.name: Spruitdrift
appellations.summary: An irrigated ward on the lower Olifants River near Vredendal. Its grapes go mostly to the large Namaqua Wines cellar, for inexpensive whites and reds, and the hot, dry valley floor depends on irrigation from the Clanwilliam Dam.

appellations.name: Ceres Plateau
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: A high plateau north-east of Ceres at about 1,000 m, apple and pear country whose cool vineyards supply sought-after Chenin and Pinot to Cape producers. It is one of the coldest wine districts in the Western Cape, with snow in winter.

appellations.name: Ceres
appellations.summary: A ward in the Ceres valley and plateau, high and cold in winter. Its high, cool vineyards produce Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Blanc prized for freshness, and the district is otherwise known for apples and pears.

appellations.name: Nuveld-Karoo
appellations.summary: A district on the high Karoo plateau inland of the Cape fold mountains, listed on the February 2026 schedule with no wards. Its vineyards are among the most remote in South Africa.

appellations.name: Prince Albert
appellations.summary: A district around the Karoo town of Prince Albert below the Swartberg, with the wards Kweekvallei, Prince Albert Valley and Swartberg. Its few vineyards make small volumes for local producers.

appellations.name: Kweekvallei
appellations.summary: A small ward near Prince Albert in the Karoo. Its irrigated vineyards grow small quantities of Shiraz and other reds in a hot, dry climate at the foot of the Swartberg mountains.

appellations.name: Prince Albert Valley
appellations.summary: A ward in the valley around Prince Albert, a hot, dry Karoo town at the foot of the Swartberg Pass. Its few hectares of vines are irrigated from mountain streams.

appellations.name: Swartberg
appellations.summary: A ward in the Swartberg mountains above Prince Albert. Its few hectares of vines grow in a dry, high-altitude setting where cold nights preserve acidity.

appellations.name: Cederberg
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A stand-alone ward in the Cederberg wilderness, with some of South Africa's highest and remotest vineyards at about 950 to 1,100 m. The Nieuwoudt family's Cederberg Private Cellar at Dwarsrivier, planted in the 1970s, makes crisp Sauvignon, Chenin and Shiraz.
appellations.terroir: Sandy soils from Table Mountain sandstone; cold winters with snow, hot dry summers.

appellations.name: Nieuwoudtville
appellations.summary: A ward around the town of Nieuwoudtville on the Bokkeveld plateau, known for spring wild flowers, at the north-western edge of the Cape. Its vineyards are cool and high, at about 750 m.

appellations.name: Leipoldtville-Sandveld
appellations.summary: A ward in the sandy coastal plain (Sandveld) around Leipoldtville, west of Clanwilliam. Its sandy soils and cool Atlantic influence suit Sauvignon Blanc and Chenin Blanc.

appellations.name: Sutherland-Karoo
appellations.summary: A high-altitude, semi-arid district around Sutherland, South Africa's coldest town and home of the national astronomical observatory, with vineyards at about 1,500 m, the highest in the country.
appellations.terroir: Dolerite and shale soils; extreme cold in winter.

appellations.name: Central Orange River
appellations.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Muscat d'Alexandrie, Pinotage, Shiraz
appellations.summary: The most northerly winegrowing area of the Cape, along about 350 km of the Orange River around Upington, Keimoes and Kakamas. Changed from a ward to a district after a 2019 proposal, it has five wards. About 6,000 ha are planted, largely for white wine, using high hut, gable and T-trellises that shade the grapes; vineyards on river islands are cooled by the water.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial river soils; very hot and arid, fully irrigated.

appellations.name: Groblershoop
appellations.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Groblershoop in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

appellations.name: Grootdrink
appellations.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Grootdrink in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

appellations.name: Kakamas
appellations.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Kakamas in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

appellations.name: Keimoes
appellations.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Keimoes in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

appellations.name: Upington
appellations.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Upington in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

appellations.name: Douglas
appellations.summary: A district around Douglas, near the confluence of the Orange and Vaal rivers, with irrigated vineyards. Like the Central Orange River vineyards, it depends on irrigation in a hot, arid climate.

appellations.name: Hartswater
appellations.summary: A ward in the Vaalharts irrigation scheme in the far north of the Northern Cape. The scheme, one of the largest in the southern hemisphere, grows grain, pecans and grapes.

appellations.name: Prieska
appellations.summary: A ward around Prieska on the Orange River. Its hot, dry vineyards are irrigated from the river and grow mainly white grapes for local cellars.

appellations.name: St Francis Bay
appellations.summary: The Eastern Cape's only ward, near the coastal resort of St Francis Bay. Its cool maritime climate suits Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.

appellations.name: Central Drakensberg
appellations.summary: A district in the foothills of the Drakensberg near Winterton. Its vineyards at about 1,000 m face summer rainfall and hail.

appellations.name: Lions River
appellations.summary: A district in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands near Howick, at about 1,000 to 1,200 m. Summer rainfall makes viticulture challenging, but cool nights suit Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

appellations.name: Rietrivier FS
appellations.summary: A ward on the Riet River near Jacobsdal in the Free State, home of the Landzicht cellar. It is one of the few demarcated wine areas in South Africa's interior.

appellations.name: Lanseria
appellations.summary: A ward near Lanseria, north-west of Johannesburg in Gauteng, listed under no geographical unit on the February 2026 schedule; it is one of the few demarcated wine areas in South Africa's interior highveld.

appellations.name: Helan Mountain East Foothill
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Marselan, Cabernet Gernischt, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling
appellations.summary:
China's best-known wine GI, covering the gravelly alluvial fans along the eastern foot of the Helan Mountains in Ningxia, from Shizuishan through Yinchuan's Xixia district, Yongning and Qingtongxia to Hongsipu. In 2026 it had about 606,000 mu (40,400 ha) of vines and 131 wineries, by its own count nearly 40 percent of China's estate vineyard. The GI was among four Chinese wine names protected in Europe when the EU-China agreement came into force in March 2021.

The region's rise has been rapid. The provincial government reclaimed desert for vineyards from the late 1990s, and small estates arrived in the 2000s: Silver Heights (Emma Gao, trained in Bordeaux), Helan Qingxue (whose Jiabeilan 2009, made with consultant Li Demei, won a Decanter international trophy in 2011), Kanaan, Domaine Pushang, Chateau Yuanshi and Chateau Hedong. Big groups followed: Changyu built Chateau Changyu Moser XV with Austrian Lenz Moser, Great Wall built Tianfu, and Moët Hennessy opened Chandon Ningxia for sparkling wine in 2013. The region's five-tier estate classification, begun in 2013, has nine Second Growths as of 2021 and no First Growth yet.

The wines are typically ripe but fresh Bordeaux blends and Cabernet Sauvignon, with polished tannins, plus Marselan, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. The challenge is the climate: winters reach minus 20 degrees C or colder, so vines are buried under soil from November to April, which limits vine age and adds cost.
appellations.terroir: Altitude about 1,100 to 1,200 m; roughly 200 mm of annual rain and 3,000 hours of sun; large day-night temperature swings. Gravelly, sandy alluvial fans with some loess, low in organic matter; irrigation from the Yellow River.
appellations.nerd_note: Burying vines each winter means many Ningxia vineyards are trained with a slanted trunk ('crawling' or 'Ningxia-style' training) so the vine can be bent over and covered with soil.

appellations.name: Yantai
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Gernischt, Merlot, Marselan, Chardonnay, Petit Manseng
appellations.summary: The GI for wine from Yantai on the Jiaodong Peninsula, the birthplace of modern Chinese wine. Zhang Bishi founded Changyu here in 1892 and dug its Grand Cellar beside the sea. Today Yantai (with the Penglai district) has the largest concentration of wineries in China, from Changyu's headquarters and its Chateau Changyu-Castel to Domaines Barons de Rothschild's Long Dai in the Qiushan valley. Its maritime climate spares vines from burial but brings monsoon rain at harvest, so wines are typically lighter and fresher than Ningxia's.
appellations.terroir: Hilly, granite- and sand-based soils near the Bohai and Yellow Sea; mild winters, humid summers.
appellations.nerd_note: Changyu's Cabernet Gernischt, a grape it imported in the 1890s, turned out on DNA testing to be Carmenère, which also went unrecognised in Chile until 1994.

appellations.name: Shacheng
appellations.grapes: Longyan (Dragon's Eye), Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The GI for the Huailai basin around Shacheng town in Hebei, north-west of Beijing behind the Great Wall, along the Sanggan River and Guanting Reservoir. The state-owned Great Wall winery (founded 1983, now COFCO) is based here, and the area's centuries-old Longyan (Dragon's Eye) grape makes its traditional dry white. Newer estates such as Chateau Sungod and Great Wall Sanggan produce Bordeaux-style reds, and the Sino-French demonstration farm of 2001, now Domaine Franco-Chinois, brought Marselan to China.
appellations.terroir: Dry, sunny and windy valley at about 500 m; cold winters require vine burial; sandy loam soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Great Wall's dry white made from Longyan in the late 1970s, the result of a state research project, is usually cited as China's first modern dry white wine.

appellations.name: Changli
appellations.summary: A coastal producing area near Qinhuangdao on the Bohai Sea, protected as a national GI. It holds the Huaxia Great Wall winery, whose Cabernet was one of China's first serious varietal reds.
appellations.terroir: Sandy soils near the coast; maritime climate with summer monsoon rain.

appellations.name: Huanren Icewine
appellations.summary: A GI for icewine from Huanren County in Liaoning, near the North Korean border, where grapes (mostly Vidal) are left on the vine to freeze and pressed while frozen, concentrating sugar and acid. Changyu's Golden Icewine Valley on Hanlong Lake is the best-known producer. It is one of four Chinese wine GIs protected in the EU.
appellations.terroir: Cold continental winters with a moderating lake; vineyards at about 380 m.

appellations.name: Yanqi Basin
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Marselan, Merlot, Riesling, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A basin on the southern side of the Tianshan near Bosten Lake and Korla, at about 1,000 to 1,200 m, which since the 2010s has become Xinjiang's leading quality area. Tiansai Vineyards and Chateau Zhongfei make structured, sunny reds. Hoxud County, in the basin, was proposed as a national GI in 2015.
appellations.terroir: Desert continental climate, gravel and sandy soils, Tianshan snowmelt irrigation; vines buried in winter.

appellations.name: Tianshan North Foothills
appellations.summary: Vineyards along the northern foothills of the Tianshan around Changji, Manas and Shihezi, including CITIC Guoan's Suntime and Xinjiang Changyu's Baron Balboa estate. Large state-farm plantings from the 1970s supply both big brands and newer estates.
appellations.terroir: Continental desert with hot summers and severe winters; alluvial soils; snowmelt irrigation.

appellations.name: Turpan
appellations.grapes: Thompson Seedless, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The Turpan depression, partly below sea level and one of the hottest places in Asia, has grown grapes for over 2,000 years; its raisins and seedless table grapes are famous throughout China. The Tang dynasty learned winemaking here after conquering Gaochang in 641. A small modern wine industry includes Loulan and Puchang; Turpan was proposed for national GI protection in 2015.
appellations.terroir: Extremely hot, arid depression (summer highs above 45 degrees C), irrigated by karez underground canals; sandy soils.

appellations.name: Shangri-La (Deqin)
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Syrah
appellations.summary: High valleys of the upper Mekong and Jinsha rivers in Deqin County, under the sacred Meili Snow Mountains, where small vineyards at 2,200 to 2,600 m produce China's most expensive wine, LVMH's Ao Yun, a Cabernet-led blend first released (2013 vintage) in 2016. French missionaries first planted vines at Cizhong church in the nineteenth century.
appellations.terroir: Dry valleys in the Himalayan rain shadow, strong sun, cold nights; river gravel and schist. Villages ripen weeks apart because of altitude and aspect.

appellations.name: Hexi Corridor
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling
appellations.summary: A narrow Silk Road corridor through Gansu between the Qilian Mountains and the Gobi, through Wuwei (ancient Liangzhou, whose wine Tang poets praised), Zhangye and Jiayuguan. Modern vineyards, buried each winter, supply wineries such as Mogao and Ziyuan.
appellations.terroir: Arid, continental and high (1,400 to 1,800 m); snowmelt irrigation; loess and gravel.

appellations.name: Yamanashi
appellations.grapes: Koshu, Muscat Bailey A, Merlot, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary:
Japan's first wine Geographical Indication, designated by the National Tax Agency in 2013, covers all of Yamanashi prefecture. Its rules require 100 percent Yamanashi grapes from listed varieties (led by Koshu and Muscat Bailey A, with European vinifera), minimum natural sugar levels and limits on chaptalisation, and wines must pass a tasting panel. In practice it is the GI for Koshu: the pale, low-alcohol white grown mostly in the eastern Kofu basin around Katsunuma.

Yamanashi has about 80 wineries, from Château Mercian (whose roots go back to 1877) and Grace Wine (Chuo Budoshu, founded 1923, where Ayana Misawa makes acclaimed Koshu and sparkling) to small new growers. Its Koshu ranges from crisp and citrusy to sur lie, barrel-aged, sparkling and skin-contact styles; its Muscat Bailey A gives light, fruity reds; and Merlot and Cabernet from the drier slopes are increasingly serious.
appellations.terroir: The Kofu basin is ringed by mountains (Mount Fuji to the south) that block some rain; summers are hot and humid. Vineyards occupy alluvial fans and slopes at 300 to 700 m, often on traditional high pergolas (tanazukuri). Akeno and Hokuto in the north-west are higher and sunnier.
appellations.nerd_note: Koshu DNA analysis (Goto-Yamamoto et al., 2015) found it is mostly vinifera with some ancestry from wild East Asian Vitis, including Vitis davidii, which may help it cope with humidity.

appellations.name: Hokkaido
appellations.grapes: Kerner, Pinot Noir, Zweigelt, Müller-Thurgau, Chardonnay, Yamabudo
appellations.summary: Japan's second wine GI, designated in 2018, covering the whole of Hokkaido. The island's cool climate, with almost no rainy season and few typhoons, suits German and Burgundian varieties. Yoichi, west of Otaru, is the leading area: Takahiko Soga, who trained at Coco Farm in Tochigi, set up there in 2010, and Domaine Takahiko's Nana-Tsu-Mori Pinot Noir, made with whole bunches and little intervention, became the most sought-after Japanese red, inspiring dozens of new growers. In 2017 the Burgundy family estate Domaine de Montille bought land near Hakodate to make Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
appellations.terroir: Cool (around 1,000 to 1,300 growing degree days in the main areas), with heavy winter snow that insulates vines; volcanic and alluvial soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Ikeda town's Tokachi Wine, founded in 1963, was Japan's first municipally owned winery and still runs a 'wine castle' that ages wine in cellars.

appellations.name: Yamagata
appellations.grapes: Delaware, Chardonnay, Merlot, Muscat Bailey A, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: A wine GI designated in 2021 for Yamagata prefecture in northern Honshu, a fruit region whose about 15 wineries make wines from European and American varieties, notably sparkling and still Delaware. Takahata Winery and Sakai Winery (founded 1892, among the oldest in Japan) are leading producers.
appellations.terroir: Inland basins with hot summers and snowy winters.

appellations.name: Osaka
